results.title: What’s new in Cluinn: updates and release notes
results.content:
### Talk, and it's written

Hold one key, say the thing, and clean text lands in whatever you were already looking at — an email, a Slack reply, a doc, a comment. Nothing to switch to, no transcript to copy out. It punctuates, it corrects itself as it goes, and you can teach it the names and words you actually use.

### An assistant that sits in the call with you

Cluinn follows your meetings and answers on the spot: the figure you can't recall, the objection you didn't see coming, the acronym the other side just dropped. On your screen, and nobody else's.

### Your recap, before you've closed the window

Summary, decisions and to-dos, written the second you hang up. Every call stays searchable afterwards, and you can ask it questions in plain language.

### How to start [...] ## Get Cluinn on your Mac

Cluinn runs on Macs with Apple silicon (M1 or later). We’ll email you the link so you can install it there.

We don’t keep your email after sending it.

# What’s new The bigger changes to Cluinn, explained.

Cluinn updates itself. These are the changes worth knowing about.

## Plans, simplified — and your Mac does the transcribing

### Two plans, and one way to try everything

Basic is dictation. Pro is dictation plus Calls — the live panel during a meeting, the saved transcript, and everything you can ask a call afterwards. [...] ### Your Mac does the transcribing

Cluinn transcribes on your own Mac wherever it can: on a recent Apple Silicon Mac with an active plan, your speech becomes text on the machine itself — no external speech model, no audio uploaded. On an Intel Mac, during a trial, or any time Cluinn can't run the on-device model, the audio is sent to our servers to be turned into text and discarded straight after.

Nothing to switch on, and nothing to choose. Cluinn uses the machine when the machine can do it.

## Cluinn is here.

An illustration of someone at a desk, headphones on, leaning back with their eyes closed.

Cluinn is out. It has spent a long time in private hands getting quietly good at three things — and today all three are yours.

results.content: What Is Cluinn? Cluinn is a Mac desktop application that combines voice-to-text dictation with a live call assistant. It works during video calls on platforms like Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams without adding bots to meetings or uploading call audio to servers.
